import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Halperin conjecture

Suppose that $F \to E \to B$ is a fibration of simply connected spaces such that $F$ is
rationally elliptic (both $H_*(F; \mathbb{Q})$ and $\pi_*(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ are
finite-dimensional) and $\chi(F) \neq 0$ (i.e. $F$ has non-zero Euler characteristic). Then the
Serre spectral sequence associated to the fibration collapses at the $E_2$ page.

Here the Serre spectral sequence is the one for cohomology with rational coefficients. Its
collapse at $E_2$ is equivalent to the fibration being *totally non-cohomologous to zero* (TNCZ),
i.e. to the fibre inclusion $j \colon F \to E$ inducing a surjection
$j^* \colon H^*(E; \mathbb{Q}) \to H^*(F; \mathbb{Q})$ (see [Lu97], §1). Since $\mathbb{Q}$ is a
field, $H^n(-; \mathbb{Q})$ is the linear dual of $H_n(-; \mathbb{Q})$, so this is in turn
equivalent to the injectivity of $j_* \colon H_n(F; \mathbb{Q}) \to H_n(E; \mathbb{Q})$ in every
degree $n$. This is the form in which the conjecture is stated below, using Mathlib's singular
homology `AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor` with rational coefficients.

"Fibration" means Serre fibration, and the fibre is $F = p^{-1}(b)$ for a point $b$ of the base.
[Lu97] works with simply connected CW complexes of finite rational type; following the Wikipedia
statement (and Meier's formulation "for arbitrary base space $B$", [Lu97, Theorem 1.5]), no
finiteness hypothesis is imposed on $E$ or $B$ here.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halperin_conjecture)
- [Lu97] G. Lupton, *Variations on a conjecture of Halperin*, Homotopy and Geometry
  (Warsaw, 1997), Banach Center Publ. 45 (1998), 115–135.
  [arXiv:math/0010124](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0010124)
-/
namespace HalperinConjecture
open CategoryTheory AlgebraicTopology Topology unitInterval
open scoped DirectSum TensorProduct

abbrev rationalHomology (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (n : ℕ) : ModuleCat ℚ :=
  ((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).obj (TopCat.of X)
blocks.docstring:
The `n`-th rational singular homology group $H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a topological
space `X`, as a `ℚ`-module.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor` (used directly; it is a functor with generic coefficients, no specialization to ℚ exists).
justification.name: HalperinConjecture.rationalHomology
justification.why_needed: Convenient abbreviation for H_n(X;ℚ) as a ℚ-module, `((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).obj (TopCat.of X)`, used in several hypotheses and the conclusion.

blocks.name: rationalHomology

/-- The `n`-th rational singular homology group $H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a topological
space `X`, as a `ℚ`-module. -/
abbrev rationalHomology (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (n : ℕ) : ModuleCat ℚ :=
  ((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).obj (TopCat.of X)

blocks.code:
abbrev rationalHomologyMap {X Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (f : C(X, Y))
    (n : ℕ) : rationalHomology X n ⟶ rationalHomology Y n :=
  ((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).map (TopCat.ofHom f)
blocks.docstring:
The map $f_* \colon H_n(X; \mathbb{Q}) \to H_n(Y; \mathbb{Q})$ induced on rational singular
homology by a continuous map `f : X → Y`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Functor.map` of `singularHomologyFunctor` applied to `TopCat.ofHom f` (this is exactly what it abbreviates).
justification.name: HalperinConjecture.rationalHomologyMap
justification.why_needed: The induced map f_* on H_n(-;ℚ) of a continuous map, needed to state injectivity of the fibre inclusion on homology.

blocks.name: rationalHomologyMap
blocks.text:
/-- The map $f_* \colon H_n(X; \mathbb{Q}) \to H_n(Y; \mathbb{Q})$ induced on rational singular
homology by a continuous map `f : X → Y`. -/
abbrev rationalHomologyMap {X Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (f : C(X, Y))
    (n : ℕ) : rationalHomology X n ⟶ rationalHomology Y n :=
  ((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).map (TopCat.ofHom f)

def eulerCharacteristic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : ℤ :=
  ∑ᶠ n : ℕ, (-1 : ℤ) ^ n * Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology X n)
blocks.docstring:
The (rational) *Euler characteristic*
$\chi(X) = \sum_n (-1)^n \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a topological space `X`.
This is the intended value when the total rational homology of `X` is finite-dimensional
(for instance when `X` is rationally elliptic); otherwise it is a junk value.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Searched Mathlib for `eulerChar`/`EulerCharacteristic`; only unrelated notions exist (none for spaces or chain complexes).
justification.name: HalperinConjecture.eulerCharacteristic
justification.why_needed: χ(F) = Σ (-1)^n dim H_n(F;ℚ); Mathlib has no Euler characteristic of a topological space.

blocks.name: eulerCharacteristic
blocks.text:
/-- The (rational) *Euler characteristic*
$\chi(X) = \sum_n (-1)^n \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a topological space `X`.
This is the intended value when the total rational homology of `X` is finite-dimensional
(for instance when `X` is rationally elliptic); otherwise it is a junk value. -/
def eulerCharacteristic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : ℤ :=
  ∑ᶠ n : ℕ, (-1 : ℤ) ^ n * Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology X n)

blocks.docstring:
A simply connected topological space `X` is *rationally elliptic* if both its total rational
homology $H_*(X; \mathbb{Q}) = \bigoplus_n H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ and its total rational homotopy
$\pi_*(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = \bigoplus_{n \ge 2} \pi_n(X, x) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ are
finite-dimensional. Only the homotopy groups $\pi_n$ with $n \ge 2$ are used since for a simply
connected space $\pi_1$ is trivial and $\pi_0$ is a point; the base point `x` is arbitrary since
`X` is path connected.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `HomotopyGroup`/`π_` notation and `Module.Finite ℚ` on `ℚ ⊗[ℤ] Additive (π_ (n+2) X x)` and on direct sums, combined into the definition.
justification.name: HalperinConjecture.IsRationallyElliptic
justification.why_needed: Rational ellipticity (dim H_*(X;ℚ) < ∞ and dim π_*(X)⊗ℚ < ∞) is absent from Mathlib and the repo.

blocks.name: IsRationallyElliptic
blocks.text:
/-- A simply connected topological space `X` is *rationally elliptic* if both its total rational
homology $H_*(X; \mathbb{Q}) = \bigoplus_n H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ and its total rational homotopy
$\pi_*(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = \bigoplus_{n \ge 2} \pi_n(X, x) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ are
finite-dimensional. Only the homotopy groups $\pi_n$ with $n \ge 2$ are used since for a simply
connected space $\pi_1$ is trivial and $\pi_0$ is a point; the base point `x` is arbitrary since
`X` is path connected. -/
def IsRationallyElliptic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  Module.Finite ℚ (⨁ n, rationalHomology X n) ∧
    ∀ x : X, Module.Finite ℚ (⨁ n, ℚ ⊗[ℤ] Additive (π_ (n + 2) X x))

blocks.code:
def IsSerreFibration {E B : Type*} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B] (p : C(E, B)) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : C(Fin n → I, E)) (H : C(I × (Fin n → I), B)), (∀ y, H (0, y) = p (f y)) →
    ∃ H' : C(I × (Fin n → I), E), (∀ y, H' (0, y) = f y) ∧ ∀ z, p (H' z) = H z
blocks.docstring:
A continuous map `p : E → B` is a *Serre fibration* if it has the homotopy lifting property
with respect to all cubes $I^n$, $n \ge 0$: for every continuous `f : Iⁿ → E` and every homotopy
`H : I × Iⁿ → B` starting at `p ∘ f`, there is a homotopy `H' : I × Iⁿ → E` starting at `f` that
lifts `H`, i.e. `p ∘ H' = H`.

justification.name: HalperinConjecture.IsSerreFibration
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no Serre or Hurewicz fibrations for topological spaces (only covering maps have a homotopy lifting theorem; `HasLiftingProperty` is categorical and would still need the cube inclusions).

blocks.name: IsSerreFibration
blocks.text:
/-- A continuous map `p : E → B` is a *Serre fibration* if it has the homotopy lifting property
with respect to all cubes $I^n$, $n \ge 0$: for every continuous `f : Iⁿ → E` and every homotopy
`H : I × Iⁿ → B` starting at `p ∘ f`, there is a homotopy `H' : I × Iⁿ → E` starting at `f` that
lifts `H`, i.e. `p ∘ H' = H`. -/
def IsSerreFibration {E B : Type*} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B] (p : C(E, B)) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : C(Fin n → I, E)) (H : C(I × (Fin n → I), B)), (∀ y, H (0, y) = p (f y)) →
    ∃ H' : C(I × (Fin n → I), E), (∀ y, H' (0, y) = f y) ∧ ∀ z, p (H' z) = H z

blocks.code:
abbrev fibreInclusion {E B : Type*} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B] (p : C(E, B))
    (b : B) : C(p ⁻¹' {b}, E) :=
  ⟨Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val⟩
blocks.docstring: The inclusion $j \colon F = p^{-1}(b) \to E$ of the fibre of `p : E → B` over `b : B`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `ContinuousMap.restrict (p ⁻¹' {b}) (ContinuousMap.id E)` (equivalent; the explicit `⟨Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val⟩` is clearer).
justification.name: HalperinConjecture.fibreInclusion
justification.why_needed: The continuous inclusion p⁻¹(b) → E as a `ContinuousMap`, to apply the homology functor.

blocks.name: fibreInclusion
blocks.text:
/-- The inclusion $j \colon F = p^{-1}(b) \to E$ of the fibre of `p : E → B` over `b : B`. -/
abbrev fibreInclusion {E B : Type*} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B] (p : C(E, B))
    (b : B) : C(p ⁻¹' {b}, E) :=
  ⟨Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val⟩

@[category API, AMS 55]
theorem IsRationallyElliptic.finite_rationalHomology {X : Type} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (hX : IsRationallyElliptic X) (n : ℕ) : Module.Finite ℚ (rationalHomology X n) :=
  have := hX.1
  Module.Finite.of_surjective (DirectSum.component ℚ ℕ (fun n => rationalHomology X n) n)
    fun x => ⟨DirectSum.lof ℚ ℕ _ n x, DirectSum.component.lof_self ..⟩
blocks.docstring: A rationally elliptic space has finite-dimensional rational homology in every degree.
blocks.name: IsRationallyElliptic.finite_rationalHomology
blocks.text:

theorem IsRationallyElliptic.finite_rationalHomology {X : Type} [TopologicalSpace X]

  have := hX.1
  Module.Finite.of_surjective (DirectSum.component ℚ ℕ (fun n => rationalHomology X n) n)
    fun x => ⟨DirectSum.lof ℚ ℕ _ n x, DirectSum.component.lof_self ..⟩

@[category test, AMS 55]
theorem eulerCharacteristic_unit : eulerCharacteristic Unit = 1 := by
  have h0 : Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology Unit 0) = 1 := by
    have e : rationalHomology Unit 0 ≅ ModuleCat.of ℚ (⨁ _ : Unit, ℚ) :=
      singularHomologyFunctorZeroOfTotallyDisconnectedSpace (ModuleCat ℚ) (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)
        (TopCat.of Unit) ≪≫ ModuleCat.coprodIsoDirectSum _
    rw [e.toLinearEquiv.finrank_eq]
    simp
  have hn (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) : Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology Unit n) = 0 := by
    have : Subsingleton (rationalHomology Unit n) :=
      ModuleCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton.mp <|
        isZero_singularHomologyFunctor_of_totallyDisconnectedSpace (ModuleCat ℚ) n
          (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ) (TopCat.of Unit) hn
    exact Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton
  rw [eulerCharacteristic, finsum_eq_single _ 0 fun n hn' => by simp [hn n hn'], h0]
  simp
blocks.docstring: The Euler characteristic of a point is `1`.

@[category API, AMS 55]
theorem isSerreFibration_id (B : Type*) [TopologicalSpace B] :
    IsSerreFibration (ContinuousMap.id B) :=
  fun _ _ H hH => ⟨H, fun y => hH y, fun _ => rfl⟩
blocks.docstring: The identity map is a Serre fibration.
blocks.name: isSerreFibration_id

@[category API, AMS 55]
theorem isSerreFibration_fst (B F : Type*) [TopologicalSpace B] [TopologicalSpace F] :
    IsSerreFibration (ContinuousMap.fst : C(B × F, B)) :=
  fun _ f H hH =>
    ⟨H.prodMk (ContinuousMap.snd.comp (f.comp ContinuousMap.snd)),
      fun y => Prod.ext (hH y) rfl, fun _ => rfl⟩
blocks.docstring: The projection of a product onto one of its factors is a Serre fibration.

    ⟨H.prodMk (ContinuousMap.snd.comp (f.comp ContinuousMap.snd)),

@[category research open, AMS 55]
theorem halperin_conjecture {E B : Type} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B]
    [SimplyConnectedSpace E] [SimplyConnectedSpace B]
    (p : C(E, B)) (hp : IsSerreFibration p) (b : B) [SimplyConnectedSpace (p ⁻¹' {b})]
    (hF : IsRationallyElliptic (p ⁻¹' {b})) (hχ : eulerCharacteristic (p ⁻¹' {b}) ≠ 0) (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (rationalHomologyMap (fibreInclusion p b) n).hom := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Halperin conjecture.** Let $F \to E \xrightarrow{p} B$ be a (Serre) fibration of simply
connected spaces, with fibre $F = p^{-1}(b)$. If $F$ is rationally elliptic with Euler
characteristic $\chi(F) \neq 0$, then the rational cohomology Serre spectral sequence of the
fibration collapses at the $E_2$ page. Equivalently, the fibration is TNCZ: the fibre inclusion
$j \colon F \to E$ induces a surjection $H^*(E; \mathbb{Q}) \to H^*(F; \mathbb{Q})$, i.e.
(dually, over the field $\mathbb{Q}$) an injection $j_* \colon H_n(F; \mathbb{Q}) \to
H_n(E; \mathbb{Q})$ in every degree $n$.

H_n(E; \mathbb{Q})$ in every degree $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 55]
theorem halperin_conjecture {E B : Type} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B]
    [SimplyConnectedSpace E] [SimplyConnectedSpace B]
    (p : C(E, B)) (hp : IsSerreFibration p) (b : B) [SimplyConnectedSpace (p ⁻¹' {b})]
    (hF : IsRationallyElliptic (p ⁻¹' {b})) (hχ : eulerCharacteristic (p ⁻¹' {b}) ≠ 0) (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (rationalHomologyMap (fibreInclusion p b) n).hom := by
  sorry
end
end HalperinConjecture

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified Prop over all (Serre) fibrations of simply connected spaces (implicitly of finite rational type) with rationally elliptic fibre (dim H*(F;ℚ) < ∞ and dim π_*(F)⊗ℚ < ∞) of nonzero (equivalently, since elliptic spaces have χ ≥ 0, positive) Euler characteristic; 'collapse at E_2' refers to the rational-coefficient cohomology Serre spectral sequence and is equivalent (Lupton §1) to the fibration being TNCZ, i.e. H*(E;ℚ) → H*(F;ℚ) surjective, which is the more directly formalizable phrasing; the article's remark that Lupton reformulated the conjecture via formality is a status note, not a separately posed question.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same core content correctly (Serre fibration of simply connected spaces via cube/disk homotopy lifting, strict fibre p⁻¹(b), rational ellipticity as finite total rational homology + finite total rationalized π_{≥2}, χ(F) ≠ 0 via alternating sum of rational Betti numbers, and collapse at E_2 rendered as the equivalent TNCZ condition, dualized over ℚ to injectivity of H_n(F;ℚ) → H_n(E;ℚ)). c01 was chosen as the base because its definitions are the cleanest (Module.Finite of the direct sum for 'finite total dimension'), it has the most careful docstrings, and it includes genuine API/test lemmas (χ(point) = 1 proved from Mathlib's singular homology; id and product projections are Serre fibrations) that validate the bespoke definitions. Edits: removed the finite-rational-type hypotheses on E and B (Lupton's paper-wide convention, not in the Wikipedia statement; Lupton's Thm 1.5 (Meier) states the conjecture 'for arbitrary base space B', so the two forms are equivalent), deleted the then-unused IsFiniteRationalType definition, and restated the API lemma as degreewise finiteness of rational homology for elliptic spaces. c03 was rejected because it imposes Mathlib CWComplex structures on E, B and on the strict fibre, an unjustified restriction not equivalent in any obvious way. c07's dual-cohomology surjectivity form is also correct but adds an extra layer; c05/c06's ULift-based universe polymorphism is correct but more complex; c08's binder style is non-idiomatic.

/-- The `n`-th rational singular homology group $H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a topological
space `X`, as a `ℚ`-module. -/
abbrev rationalHomology (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (n : ℕ) : ModuleCat ℚ :=
  ((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).obj (TopCat.of X)

/-- The map $f_* \colon H_n(X; \mathbb{Q}) \to H_n(Y; \mathbb{Q})$ induced on rational singular
homology by a continuous map `f : X → Y`. -/
abbrev rationalHomologyMap {X Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (f : C(X, Y))
    (n : ℕ) : rationalHomology X n ⟶ rationalHomology Y n :=
  ((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)).map (TopCat.ofHom f)

/-- The (rational) *Euler characteristic*
$\chi(X) = \sum_n (-1)^n \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a topological space `X`.
This is the intended value when the total rational homology of `X` is finite-dimensional
(for instance when `X` is rationally elliptic); otherwise it is a junk value. -/
def eulerCharacteristic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : ℤ :=
  ∑ᶠ n : ℕ, (-1 : ℤ) ^ n * Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology X n)

/-- A simply connected topological space `X` is *rationally elliptic* if both its total rational
homology $H_*(X; \mathbb{Q}) = \bigoplus_n H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ and its total rational homotopy
$\pi_*(X) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = \bigoplus_{n \ge 2} \pi_n(X, x) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ are
finite-dimensional. Only the homotopy groups $\pi_n$ with $n \ge 2$ are used since for a simply
connected space $\pi_1$ is trivial and $\pi_0$ is a point; the base point `x` is arbitrary since
`X` is path connected. -/
def IsRationallyElliptic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  Module.Finite ℚ (⨁ n, rationalHomology X n) ∧
    ∀ x : X, Module.Finite ℚ (⨁ n, ℚ ⊗[ℤ] Additive (π_ (n + 2) X x))

/-- A continuous map `p : E → B` is a *Serre fibration* if it has the homotopy lifting property
with respect to all cubes $I^n$, $n \ge 0$: for every continuous `f : Iⁿ → E` and every homotopy
`H : I × Iⁿ → B` starting at `p ∘ f`, there is a homotopy `H' : I × Iⁿ → E` starting at `f` that
lifts `H`, i.e. `p ∘ H' = H`. -/
def IsSerreFibration {E B : Type*} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B] (p : C(E, B)) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : C(Fin n → I, E)) (H : C(I × (Fin n → I), B)), (∀ y, H (0, y) = p (f y)) →
    ∃ H' : C(I × (Fin n → I), E), (∀ y, H' (0, y) = f y) ∧ ∀ z, p (H' z) = H z

/-- The inclusion $j \colon F = p^{-1}(b) \to E$ of the fibre of `p : E → B` over `b : B`. -/
abbrev fibreInclusion {E B : Type*} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B] (p : C(E, B))
    (b : B) : C(p ⁻¹' {b}, E) :=
  ⟨Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val⟩

/-- A rationally elliptic space has finite-dimensional rational homology in every degree. -/
@[category API, AMS 55]
theorem IsRationallyElliptic.finite_rationalHomology {X : Type} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (hX : IsRationallyElliptic X) (n : ℕ) : Module.Finite ℚ (rationalHomology X n) :=
  have := hX.1
  Module.Finite.of_surjective (DirectSum.component ℚ ℕ (fun n => rationalHomology X n) n)
    fun x => ⟨DirectSum.lof ℚ ℕ _ n x, DirectSum.component.lof_self ..⟩

/-- The Euler characteristic of a point is `1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 55]
theorem eulerCharacteristic_unit : eulerCharacteristic Unit = 1 := by
  have h0 : Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology Unit 0) = 1 := by
    have e : rationalHomology Unit 0 ≅ ModuleCat.of ℚ (⨁ _ : Unit, ℚ) :=
      singularHomologyFunctorZeroOfTotallyDisconnectedSpace (ModuleCat ℚ) (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ)
        (TopCat.of Unit) ≪≫ ModuleCat.coprodIsoDirectSum _
    rw [e.toLinearEquiv.finrank_eq]
    simp
  have hn (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) : Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology Unit n) = 0 := by
    have : Subsingleton (rationalHomology Unit n) :=
      ModuleCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton.mp <|
        isZero_singularHomologyFunctor_of_totallyDisconnectedSpace (ModuleCat ℚ) n
          (ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ) (TopCat.of Unit) hn
    exact Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton
  rw [eulerCharacteristic, finsum_eq_single _ 0 fun n hn' => by simp [hn n hn'], h0]
  simp

/-- The identity map is a Serre fibration. -/
@[category API, AMS 55]
theorem isSerreFibration_id (B : Type*) [TopologicalSpace B] :
    IsSerreFibration (ContinuousMap.id B) :=
  fun _ _ H hH => ⟨H, fun y => hH y, fun _ => rfl⟩

/-- The projection of a product onto one of its factors is a Serre fibration. -/
@[category API, AMS 55]
theorem isSerreFibration_fst (B F : Type*) [TopologicalSpace B] [TopologicalSpace F] :
    IsSerreFibration (ContinuousMap.fst : C(B × F, B)) :=
  fun _ f H hH =>
    ⟨H.prodMk (ContinuousMap.snd.comp (f.comp ContinuousMap.snd)),
      fun y => Prod.ext (hH y) rfl, fun _ => rfl⟩

/--
**Halperin conjecture.** Let $F \to E \xrightarrow{p} B$ be a (Serre) fibration of simply
connected spaces, with fibre $F = p^{-1}(b)$. If $F$ is rationally elliptic with Euler
characteristic $\chi(F) \neq 0$, then the rational cohomology Serre spectral sequence of the
fibration collapses at the $E_2$ page. Equivalently, the fibration is TNCZ: the fibre inclusion
$j \colon F \to E$ induces a surjection $H^*(E; \mathbb{Q}) \to H^*(F; \mathbb{Q})$, i.e.
(dually, over the field $\mathbb{Q}$) an injection $j_* \colon H_n(F; \mathbb{Q}) \to
H_n(E; \mathbb{Q})$ in every degree $n$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 55]
theorem halperin_conjecture {E B : Type} [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B]
    [SimplyConnectedSpace E] [SimplyConnectedSpace B]
    (p : C(E, B)) (hp : IsSerreFibration p) (b : B) [SimplyConnectedSpace (p ⁻¹' {b})]
    (hF : IsRationallyElliptic (p ⁻¹' {b})) (hχ : eulerCharacteristic (p ⁻¹' {b}) ≠ 0) (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (rationalHomologyMap (fibreInclusion p b) n).hom := by
  sorry

end

end HalperinConjecture

items: Conclusion: 'Serre spectral sequence collapses at E_2' is formalized as TNCZ (Lupton §1, citing McCleary Thm 5.9), and TNCZ (j^* : H^*(E;ℚ) → H^*(F;ℚ) surjective) is further rephrased as injectivity of j_* : H_n(F;ℚ) → H_n(E;ℚ) in every degree. Over the field ℚ, H^n(-;ℚ) is naturally the linear dual of H_n(-;ℚ) (universal coefficients) and a linear map between vector spaces is injective iff its transpose is surjective, so this is an exact equivalence with no finiteness needed. Mathlib has singular homology but neither singular cohomology nor spectral sequences.

Rational homology is Mathlib's `singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat ℚ) n` with coefficient object `ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ`; the chain complex is then ℚ[Sing_n X] (checked by `rfl` in a scratch file), i.e. genuine singular homology with ℚ coefficients. Because this coefficient object lives in `Type`, all spaces in the main statement are taken in `Type` (universe 0), as in other files of the collection (e.g. BingBorsuk).

'Fibration' is taken to mean Serre fibration (homotopy lifting property for all cubes I^n, n ≥ 0), the convention of Félix–Halperin–Thomas and the setting in which the Serre spectral sequence exists; this is the most general reading and implies the Hurewicz-fibration version. Bespoke `IsSerreFibration` defined on `C(E, B)`.

The fibre is F = p⁻¹(b) for a chosen point b : B (with the subspace topology); since B is simply connected (hence path connected) the choice of b is immaterial for a Serre fibration. Hypotheses on F (simply connected, rationally elliptic, χ ≠ 0) are imposed on this literal fibre.

Following Lupton's standing convention ('all spaces are simply connected ... of finite type over ℚ') and the decomposition notes, E and B are assumed of finite rational type (`IsFiniteRationalType`: each H_n(-;ℚ) finite-dimensional). The hypothesis on E is redundant (follows from B and F via the Serre spectral sequence) and F's is implied by ellipticity (proved as the API lemma `IsRationallyElliptic.isFiniteRationalType`); the conjecture is also believed equivalent without these (pullback from the finite-type classifying space Baut_1(F)), so they are harmless but a reviewer may prefer to drop them to match Wikipedia literally.

Spaces are arbitrary topological spaces rather than CW complexes; this is equivalent up to CW approximation since all invariants used are weak-homotopy invariants and a pullback of a Serre fibration along a weak equivalence of bases is a weak equivalence on total spaces with the same fibre.

`IsRationallyElliptic X` := the total rational homology ⨁_n H_n(X;ℚ) is a finite-dimensional ℚ-module, and for every basepoint x the total rational homotopy ⨁_{n≥0} ℚ ⊗[ℤ] Additive(π_{n+2}(X,x)) is finite-dimensional. Only π_n for n ≥ 2 is used, which is correct for simply connected X (π_1 = 0, π_0 a point); the definition is only meant for simply connected spaces, as documented. Quantifying over all basepoints is equivalent to a single one for path-connected X.

`eulerCharacteristic X` := ∑ᶠ n, (-1)^n · finrank_ℚ H_n(X;ℚ) : ℤ, using homology Betti numbers (equal to cohomology Betti numbers over ℚ). It is the true Euler characteristic whenever total rational homology is finite-dimensional, which is guaranteed by the ellipticity hypothesis on F; elsewhere it is a junk value (documented). Tested: `eulerCharacteristic Unit = 1`.
The hypothesis χ(F) ≠ 0 is taken literally as in Wikipedia (equivalent to χ(F) > 0 for elliptic F by Halperin's theorem, but the literal form is used).
The conclusion is stated for a universally quantified degree `n : ℕ` as a theorem parameter, i.e. injectivity in every degree, which is the full TNCZ condition.

reviewer_notes: Modeling choices a reviewer should know: (1) 'Serre spectral sequence collapses at E_2' is not directly expressible (Mathlib has no spectral sequences or singular cohomology); it is stated in the standard equivalent TNCZ form (Lupton §1, McCleary Thm 5.9), further dualized over the field ℚ to injectivity of the fibre inclusion on rational singular homology in every degree — an exact equivalence needing no finiteness. (2) 'Fibration' = Serre fibration (homotopy lifting for all cubes Iⁿ, n ≥ 0), the fibre is the strict fibre p⁻¹(b), and all three of F, E, B are required simply connected as in the source (E's is redundant). (3) Spaces live in `Type` because Mathlib's singularHomologyFunctor needs the coefficient module ℚ in the same universe; purely technical. (4) Lupton's blanket 'CW complexes of finite rational type' convention is not imposed on E, B; this follows the Wikipedia wording and Meier's formulation (Lupton Thm 1.5(1), 'arbitrary base space B'); the Der^{<0}=0 argument shows the two forms are equivalent. Candidates c01/c03/c04/c07/c08 included finite type on E,B — also acceptable, just weaker-looking. (5) χ is defined by a finsum, a junk value for spaces with infinite total rational homology, but the ellipticity hypothesis makes the support finite. (6) Rational homotopy uses only π_{n+2}, correct for simply connected F (π_0, π_1 trivial); quantifying over all basepoints is equivalent to one since F is path connected and nonempty (SimplyConnectedSpace implies Nonempty). No candidate omitted the slot; all compiled.
